name: Positive-unlabelled learning and autoencoder anomaly detection

identity.method_name: Positive-Unlabeled (PU) learning (Elkan-Noto estimator, bagging-PU / Mordelet-Vert, nnPU non-negative risk estimator) combined with fully unsupervised anomaly detection (autoencoder reconstruction error, Isolation Forest)
identity.core_idea: PU learning is the statistical frame for a dataset with some confirmed positives (documented encroachment cases) and a mass of unlabeled data that is a mixture of hidden positives and negatives, with no confirmed negatives at all: Elkan-Noto trains a classifier treating unlabeled as negative, then rescales its output by an estimated constant c = P(labeled|positive); bagging-PU (Mordelet & Vert) resamples the unlabeled set as pseudo-negatives across many bootstrap classifiers and averages; nnPU replaces the (often negative, unstable) naive risk estimator with a non-negative one so flexible models do not overfit on very few positives. Autoencoder and Isolation Forest anomaly detection are a separate, stricter-sounding but actually looser frame: they need no rare-class label at all, only a notion of a 'typical' pixel/lake-year distribution, and flag whatever deviates from it (encoder-decoder reconstruction error, or how easily a point is isolated by random splits) as anomalous, leaving the human to decide afterward whether an anomaly is encroachment, desilting, hyacinth, or noise.
identity.official_dataset_ids: Not a dataset-dependent method. Cited PU-learning benchmarks are third-party research datasets with their own names, not Earth Engine/STAC IDs: the Haute-Garonne Sentinel-2 SITS agricultural-parcel benchmark used in doi 10.3390/rs14010140, and MNIST/CIFAR-10 used as the canonical sample-size benchmark for nnPU (Kiryo et al. 2017, arXiv 1703.00593). For this project, the method would run on the project's own existing Sentinel-2/MNDWI/NDVI feature stack; no new official dataset ID is required.

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: Two distinct strategies bundled under one item. (1) Positive-unlabelled learning: treat a small set of documented Bengaluru encroachment cases (news reports, NGT/High Court/BBMP-survey findings naming specific lakes as encroached) as the positive set P, and every other lake-year as unlabeled U (a mixture of true negatives and un-reported positives, since BBMP's own 2023-24 survey found roughly 80% of surveyed lakes, 159 of 202, carry some documented encroachment -- meaning U is not 'mostly negative', it is likely mostly positive and simply unreported). Cost: no per-pixel manual annotation, but real archival effort to find, date and geolocate each case (court filings, Deccan Herald/Citizen Matters archives, BBMP/Karnataka survey reports), realistically several student-days for a yield in the single digits (see evidence). (2) Fully unsupervised anomaly detection (autoencoder, Isolation Forest): needs zero rare-class labels of any kind, costs nothing in labelling effort, but only ever outputs a generic 'this lake-year is statistically unusual' score, never an 'encroached' label -- the mapping from anomaly to encroachment must still be supplied by the same rules (MNDWI/NDVI thresholds, buffer geometry) the project already uses.
fit_to_project.input_required: Same 20 m MNDWI/NDVI/OSM feature stack the project already has for the unsupervised half. For the PU half, additionally requires a hand-built table of documented positive cases: lake name, approximate year(s) the encroachment was reported, and (ideally) an extent in acres/guntas from the source -- this table does not exist yet and must be constructed by the student from public records.
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: only-if-reframed. At the lake-year level (42 rows) there are at most 6 candidate 'positive' units (one per lake, since court/news records describe lakes, not lake-years), which is far too few to fit any PU estimator with its usual statistical guarantees. Reframed per-pixel (~900,000 pixels/scene x 6 lakes x 7 years ~ 37.8 million pixel-year observations) the unsupervised anomaly-detection half has effectively unlimited training data, but the PU half still cannot be reframed this way without inventing pixel-level 'positive' labels that the source documents never actually specify -- court records give acreage figures for a lake as of a report date, not georeferenced pixel footprints.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: needs-weak-labels for the PU half (see label_source_needed); yes for the unsupervised anomaly-detection half, which is the entire point of citing it here -- it needs no rare-class label, weak or otherwise, only a definition of 'typical'.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: Resolution-agnostic in principle: both PU estimators and autoencoder/Isolation Forest operate on whatever feature vector they are given (MNDWI, NDVI, band ratios, textures) and carry no assumption of sub-metre imagery, unlike pretrained CNN/segmentation checkpoints elsewhere in this project's shortlist. This is a genuine, if modest, advantage of this item over items that require transferring VHR-trained weights to 20 m data.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: PU half: documented Bengaluru encroachment cases from news archives (Deccan Herald, Citizen Matters, Times of India), NGT/Karnataka High Court orders, and the BBMP/Karnataka Department of Survey Settlement and Land Records encroachment surveys. Unsupervised half: none.
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: Only partially addresses (3) no real ground truth, and only for the PU half, by substituting a small, self-collected, likely biased set of weak positives -- it does not resolve the underlying absence of confirmed negatives or verified labels, it relabels the problem. The unsupervised half sidesteps limitation (3) honestly by never claiming to detect 'encroachment' at all, only 'anomaly'. Neither half addresses (1) the 42-row limit as a genuine sample-size fix, (2) the single-snapshot OpenStreetMap building layer, or (4) the dry-season-only annual scene.
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: No. Any anomaly detector trained on the lake-year feature stack will flag Bellandur's 15.7 ha (2019) -> 0.4 ha (2021) -> 107.9 ha (2025) trajectory as a large statistical outlier by construction, indistinguishable from an encroachment-driven water-area collapse unless an explicit desilting-year exclusion list (from municipal records) is supplied as a side input -- the method itself has no concept of 'planned maintenance drawdown' versus 'permanent loss'. The PU half is equally vulnerable: if a documented 'positive' case happens to coincide with a desilting year, the resulting c-estimate or class-prior is contaminated by a false positive that has nothing to do with encroachment.
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: No. A hyacinth mat flips both MNDWI (water to non-water) and NDVI (vegetation-positive) simultaneously; an autoencoder/Isolation Forest trained without an explicit macrophyte feature will treat this as a strong joint anomaly, again indistinguishable from encroachment without cross-checking against the published macrophyte-cover mapping (MDPI Remote Sensing 2020, doi 10.3390/rs12223843) for Bellandur and Varthur specifically.
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: This is the one place a document-derived positive label can, in principle, carry real legal weight: NGT orders and BBMP survey findings cite specific acreage and sometimes survey numbers (e.g. 'Tahsildar claimed 16 acres... government sources claim at least 36 acres encroached' around Bellandur). In practice this legal detail is almost never resolvable to a specific 20 m pixel set without additional cadastral georeferencing the project does not have, so the traceable unit is 'this lake, as of this report date, per this authority' -- not a buffer-specific claim. Neither the 30 m Supreme-Court-reinstated Bengaluru Master Plan buffer nor the 75 m former NGT buffer can be tested directly from acreage figures alone; the unsupervised anomaly half has zero legal traceability by construction (a statistical outlier is not a legal finding).
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: MNDWI/NDVI genuinely vary year to year and are usable inputs to either half. The PU 'positive' labels, however, are cumulative status reports as of a publication or judgment date (e.g. '36 acres encroached as of 2018'), not year-stamped events -- they cannot populate the 42 distinct lake-year rows, only a coarse 6-lake, largely static binary vector, repeating the exact single-snapshot flaw the project's own OpenStreetMap building layer already has.

implementation.libraries: scikit-learn (IsolationForest, OneClassSVM) for the classical half; PyOD (pyod.models.iforest, pyod.models.auto_encoder, pyod.models.deep_svdd) for a unified anomaly-detection API; pulearn (bagging-PU wrapper over any sklearn classifier) and a from-scratch Elkan-Noto rescaling (a few lines of NumPy) for the PU half; kiryor/nnPUlearning (reference Chainer implementation) would need re-porting to PyTorch/sklearn for practical use.
implementation.pretrained_weights: None needed or available -- both PU estimators and the anomaly detectors are fit from scratch on the project's own small feature stack each run; there is no pretrained-weight transfer-resolution problem here, unlike the CNN/segmentation items in this project's shortlist.
implementation.licence: scikit-learn (BSD-3), PyOD (BSD-2), pulearn (MIT), nnPUlearning reference code (MIT) -- all usable without restriction in an academic project.
implementation.compute_requirement: CPU-only, laptop-feasible for both halves. Fitting Isolation Forest or a small autoencoder on even the full ~37.8 million pixel-year feature stack takes minutes on a laptop CPU or a free Colab/Kaggle CPU/GPU instance; fitting Elkan-Noto/bagging-PU/nnPU on a table with a handful of positive labels is sub-second. No GPU is structurally required.
implementation.student_days: 3-5 days for a defensible Isolation Forest / autoencoder anomaly-detection baseline reusing existing features. 5-8 additional days of archival research to find, date and geolocate documented Bengaluru encroachment cases for the PU half (this is the dominant cost, not the modelling). 2-3 days to implement and honestly stress-test an Elkan-Noto or nnPU estimator on however many positives are actually found. Total 10-15 student-days, with a substantial risk that the PU half ends in a documented null result once the true positive count is known.

evaluation.metrics: For the anomaly-detection half: reconstruction-error or isolation-score ranking of lake-years, reported as an ordered list with no pretense of precision/recall (there is no ground truth to score against). For the PU half, if attempted: PU-specific estimators of precision/recall (e.g. label-frequency-adjusted recall following Elkan & Noto's own diagnostics) rather than ordinary accuracy, since ordinary accuracy is undefined without confirmed negatives and would be dominated by the unlabeled majority regardless of correctness.
evaluation.validation_protocol: leave-one-lake-out is the only defensible split for either half, given only 6 lakes; for the PU half specifically, if 4-5 of the 6 project lakes are already among Bengaluru's most publicly documented encroachment cases (Bellandur, Varthur are the canonical examples), there is effectively no genuinely held-out lake left to validate against, since almost every lake in the study is already 'known'.
evaluation.leakage_risk: The chief leakage risk is selection bias, not spatial leakage: documented positive cases are systematically the most publicized, largest, most litigated lakes, not a random sample of encroached lakes, so any PU estimator's core assumption (positives are a random subset of the true positive population, i.e. 'selected completely at random', SCAR) is very likely violated by construction. Separately, if desilting or hyacinth years are inadvertently included among the 'positive' cases, the resulting c-estimate or class prior is contaminated by a confound rather than a true positive.
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: Neither Elkan-Noto's point estimate of c nor a vanilla autoencoder/Isolation Forest score comes with a calibrated interval by default. Bagging-PU's ensemble variance, or a bootstrap over Isolation Forest's tree ensemble, gives an ad hoc uncertainty band that should be reported instead of a bare score; with single-digit positive counts this band will likely be very wide, and that width is itself an important, honestly reportable finding.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: Not applicable in the synthetic-data sense (no SMOTE/GAN/diffusion augmentation is used here), but a related risk applies to bagging-PU: repeatedly bootstrap-resampling an unlabeled set of only 6 lakes' worth of data reuses the same handful of underlying observations many times, which can manufacture an appearance of a stable ensemble consensus from a very small number of independent facts; this must be disclosed as an ensemble-variance artifact rather than as additional evidence.

evidence.published_performance: PU learning for satellite image time series (PUL-SITS, doi 10.3390/rs14010140, Remote Sensing 14(1):140, 2022): recurrent-autoencoder-based PU pipeline for cereal/forest extraction from Sentinel-2 time series over Haute-Garonne, France; the paper reports F-measure gains over classical one-class/PU baselines on an agricultural-parcel benchmark with parcel counts in the thousands to tens of thousands and hundreds-to-thousands of positive parcels per target class [verify -- exact positive/unlabeled counts could not be confirmed against the full text in this research pass, paywalled beyond abstract]. One-class remote-sensing PUL (Li, Guo & Elkan, IEEE TGRS 49(2):717-725, 2011, IEEE Xplore 5559411, and the related ensemble-based extension IEEE Xplore 8279452): classical PU classifiers on VHR/hyperspectral scenes, again using positive-sample counts in the hundreds per class [verify -- exact N not confirmed]. nnPU (Kiryo et al. 2017, arXiv 1703.00593): canonical MNIST/CIFAR-10 benchmark used np=100 positive examples against nu=59,900 unlabeled examples -- even this deliberately 'small-positive-count' benchmark used 100 positives, an order of magnitude more than the single-digit count realistically obtainable for Bengaluru lakes. Bagging-PU (Mordelet & Vert, Pattern Recognition Letters, 2014): gene-regulatory-network application with hundreds of positive genes, not a remote-sensing benchmark [verify].
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: PUL-SITS: rural agricultural Haute-Garonne, southwest France, at Sentinel-2 pixel/parcel scale -- no urban lakes, no India. Li/Guo/Elkan one-class RS PUL: US agricultural/urban VHR or hyperspectral scenes, sub-metre to a few metres resolution, not 20 m Sentinel-2. nnPU: MNIST/CIFAR-10, not remote sensing at all. None of the cited PU literature studies wetlands, lakes, or India.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: No. No evidence was found of PU learning or autoencoder/Isolation-Forest anomaly detection being applied to Bengaluru lakes or any Indian urban wetland in the literature reviewed.
evidence.evidence_recency: PUL-SITS 2022 (within window). nnPU 2017 and Elkan-Noto 2008, and Mordelet-Vert bagging-PU 2014 are all pre-2020 and are the foundational/still-standard references for their respective estimators; flagged as older evidence per the task's 2020-onward preference, though they remain the primary citable sources for these specific estimators. A 2025 isolation-forest environmental-monitoring paper (doi 10.3390/environments12040116) is recent but is a generic land-management application, not lake-encroachment-specific [verify].
evidence.primary_sources: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs14010140 ; https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/5559411 (Li, Guo & Elkan 2011) ; https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8279452 (ensemble PU one-class RS) ; https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/9201373 (one-class RS from positive and unlabeled background data) ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.00593 (Kiryo et al., nnPU) ; https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~elkan/posonly.pdf (Elkan & Noto 2008) ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167865513002432 (Mordelet & Vert, bagging-PU) ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.04547 (PUNCH, hyperspectral PU) ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0303243421003056 (DOCC, deep one-class crop PU) ; https://doi.org/10.3390/environments12040116 (Isolation Forest, environmental monitoring) ; macrophyte cross-check: https://doi.org/10.3390/rs12223843 ; Bengaluru encroachment documentation: https://www.deccanherald.com/india/karnataka/bengaluru/encroached-part-varthur-lake-belongs-2087823 ; https://citizenmatters.in/all-you-need-to-know-about-bellandur-lake-and-its-problems/ ; https://clpr.org.in/blog/bangalores-dying-lakes-where-is-the-apex-committee/ ; https://www.constructionworld.in/urban-infrastructure/wastewater-and-sewage-treatment/bengaluru-lakes-encroached-bbmp-reveals-extent/67209.

risk.failure_modes: (1) SCAR violation: documented positive cases are the most litigated, most publicized lakes, not a random sample of all encroached lakes, biasing any Elkan-Noto c-estimate or nnPU class prior; (2) sample-size gap: every PU-in-remote-sensing paper found here uses positive counts from the hundreds (Li/Guo/Elkan) into the tens of thousands of parcels (PUL-SITS), versus a realistic single-digit count for this project; (3) inverted premise: BBMP's own survey suggests ~80% of Bengaluru lakes carry documented encroachment, so the 'mass unlabeled, few positive' PU assumption may not even hold -- there may not be enough plausible negatives left among 6 famous lakes to serve as a meaningful unlabeled set; (4) desilting and hyacinth both produce large, encroachment-indistinguishable statistical anomalies for the unsupervised half; (5) documented cases are cumulative-status snapshots, not year-stamped events, so they cannot populate the 42 lake-year rows, only a coarse ~6-entry lake-level vector.
risk.panel_defensibility: The first question a panel will ask is 'how many positive examples did you actually find, and are they a random sample or just the famous ones everyone already knows about?' -- the honest answer (likely single digits, all well-known, selection-biased) directly undermines the statistical premise every cited PU paper relies on, and there is no way to answer this question that avoids admitting the estimator's assumptions are not met. A second predictable question, 'did your anomaly detector just relearn the desilting/hyacinth pattern?', has no automatic defence without an explicit exclusion list built from external records.
risk.honest_expectation: A defensible, honestly-scoped outcome is to report Isolation Forest / autoencoder anomaly scores purely as an unsupervised descriptive layer -- which lake-years are statistical outliers relative to the others -- explicitly not labelled 'encroachment', with the handful of documented cases used only as a qualitative face-validity spot-check, not as a trained classifier's test set. Attempting to fit a formal PU estimator on fewer than ten, selection-biased positives is very likely to produce an unstable, non-reproducible c-estimate or class prior that will not survive scrutiny and should be reported as a documented null result for that half of the method.

verdict.recommended_rank: reject for formal PU learning (Elkan-Noto / bagging-PU / nnPU) as a primary or defensible quantitative method, given a realistic single-digit, selection-biased positive count against a literature that needs hundreds to tens of thousands; adopt-if-time for autoencoder / Isolation Forest anomaly detection purely as an unsupervised, clearly-labelled exploratory layer alongside the existing classical baseline, with outputs never presented as validated encroachment detections.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: We could not obtain enough independently-sampled, dated positive encroachment cases (realistically single digits, all already well-known, not a random sample) to satisfy any published PU-learning estimator's assumptions, so we report that as a null result and instead use isolation-forest/autoencoder anomaly detection only as an unsupervised descriptive check, not as a trained encroachment classifier.
